items.title: Live: Financial stocks help markets rebound after 4 days; Q2 updates in focus | Closing Bell
items.description: The Nifty snaps its four-day losing streak, while the Sensex surges 400 points and the Nifty moves above the 22,500 mark. Market breadth remains weak, with declines outpacing advances, although all sectors except pharma trade in the green. Pharma stocks extend their selloff for a third straight day, while PSU banking stocks gain on solid Q2 updates, with Indian Bank, Bank of India and Bank of Baroda rising up to 4%. HDFC Bank shares see profit-booking after early gains, while Bajaj Finance jumps following its ₹17,500 crore fundraising plan. Retail stocks remain under pressure, with V-2 Retail hitting a 52-week low, while DMart shares slip after its Q2 update and trade near their 52-week low. Among Nifty 50 stocks, Tata Motors PV, Shriram Finance and Bajaj Finance are the top gainers, while HCL Tech, Asian Paints and Infosys are the top losers. Brent crude prices cool to around $100 a barrel, while Asian markets trade in the green, with the Nikkei 225 gaining 2% and the Hang Seng remaining flat.

items.title: Market Bottom, RBI Policy, Commodities And Financials: Rohit Srivastava's Full Outlook
items.description:
Nifty has logged eight straight weekly losses, FPIs have been heavy sellers and the rupee has been under pressure, so the big question is when the market will bottom out. In this interview, Rohit Srivastava, Founder of Indiacharts and Web.strike money, says the market could see a very strong recovery within a week. He also shares his view on the RBI policy due this week and what US bond yields mean for markets.

On where to invest, Rohit likes the commodity sector and finds it a safe place to be. Along with metals, he has agro commodities in focus and says steel is another space where you can invest. Among equity indices, he likes Bank, Realty and Auto. He also talks about the auto sector and hospital stocks.

In financials, he says the second-line banks are better than the bigger ones, and smaller names could give better returns than the large banks. He explains why the bigger returns in this space could come from there.

items.title: Quick Commerce, E-commerce, Food Delivery: Who Wins India’s Internet War? | Navin Killa, UBS
items.description:
India’s internet economy is entering its next phase — but which companies will actually capture the profit pool?
In this conversation, Navin Killa, Head of APAC at UBS, breaks down the investment landscape across India’s internet companies — from quick commerce and food delivery to beauty and value commerce.
He discusses how the pecking order could evolve, whether platform stocks still offer an attractive proposition, how long it could take for category leaders to establish themselves, and whether current margin assumptions for companies such as Eternal can hold.
The conversation also explores total addressable markets, profit pools, zero-commission models, competitive moats and the longer-term investability of internet companies.
We also discuss telecom tariffs and valuations, satellite broadband and what India’s growth-versus-valuation equation means for investors.
In this episode:
Who will win India’s quick-commerce battle?
Where will the internet profit pool accrue?
Eternal: Are steady-state margins sustainable?
Food delivery’s next competitive battleground
Is there a moat in beauty e-commerce?
Can value commerce create a new market?
Are zero-commission models disruptive?
Which internet models will dominate India?
How should investors value internet companies?
